target_customer: Developers running multiple AI coding agents in parallel on macOS
problem: Running many Claude Code or Codex sessions is hard to monitor; existing orchestrators are slow Electron or Tauri apps.
business_model: Free open source terminal with optional paid cmux Pro and a commercial license for organizations that cannot use GPL
product_category: Developer tools, terminal for coding agents

founders.name: Lawrence Chen
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; wrote the Show HN post explaining why cmux was built.

technical_complexity.rationale: Native Swift and AppKit app on libghostty with scripting and notification features, standard engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Open source GPL with a rented rendering core; community and speed are the only edges.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action was found in the sources opened.

market_need_then: The terminal product launched in February 2026 when parallel coding agents were common; the company as Manaflow began in 2024 with a different product. The need was described by the founder in the launch post.

branding.domain_note: cmux.com and cmux.dev both appear in results; history not found.

identity.logo: app icon shown on the site, details not described in sources

branding.brand_signature: Notification rings that light up panes when agents need attention
branding.community_and_virality: Show HN on 2026-02-19 peaked at number 2, shouted out by Ghostty creator Mitchell Hashimoto, viral in Japan per the company; around 21,700 GitHub stars by June 2026 per one review. Article notes at least three unrelated projects named cmux.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong developer buzz and star growth, but the name collides with other projects and no merch or wider brand evidence was found.

pivots.from: Manaflow, an open source applied AI lab with earlier devtools
pivots.why: A review says Manaflow pivoted to cmux; the founder says he built it for his own parallel agent workflow

outcome_analysis: cmux is active and has shown real developer traction after a February 2026 Show HN, helped by the timing of coding agent adoption and by free open source distribution. No funding beyond YC, no exit and no failure was found. Monetisation through cmux Pro is unproven in the sources.
notes: YC page for cmux says Summer 2024, team size 3; other YC pages for Manaflow say team size 2. Funding: Caplight and VCBacked list $500K in September 2024 led by Y Combinator, aggregator only, unverified and not recorded as a round. Competition: no sources dated near the 2024 batch exist because the product is from 2026. Google search of dated competitors (Warp, iTerm2, tmux) found only 2026 comparisons.
